headline: Local Clerk Forced To Convert Into Living Filing Cabinet To Accommodate Pending Appeals
body:
Sudhakar Rao, a junior records assistant in the state administrative office, has begun wearing custom-fitted iron shelves under his blazer and labeling his limbs alphabetically to help process the staggering backlog of 37 lakh appeals. The decision came after the office ran out of physical floor space, forcing Rao to adopt a vertical, stationary lifestyle to serve as a high-density human archive for the ongoing administrative surge.

“I’ve started categorizing the complaints by weight rather than urgency, as my left hip can comfortably hold about 400 petitions before I start to tilt,” said Rao, who now spends his lunch breaks reorganizing his pockets to ensure related grievances are filed in proximity to his collarbone. His supervisor noted that while the transition has been physically demanding, the filing system is significantly more efficient than the previous method of burying documents under half-eaten tiffin boxes.

Visitors to the office have expressed confusion as they are now required to staple their grievances directly to Rao’s coat as he stands motionless in the hallway. “I went in to appeal a property tax issue, but was told I needed to wait for the ‘G-Section’ to rotate his shoulder so I could reach the submission slot,” said local resident Ajay Verma. The office plans to install a small watering station nearby to ensure that the human filing system remains hydrated during peak processing months.
caption: Efficiency has reached new, albeit slightly uncomfortable, heights at the state administrative office. #Bureaucracy #AdministrativeHumor #WorkLifeBalance #HumanArchive (satire)
igHook: Would you trust a human filing cabinet to handle your most important paperwork?

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 7 provides the most distinct and absurd imagery—a clerk literally becoming the filing system—which elevates the premise of bureaucratic gridlock beyond the 'clerk retires' or 'mountain of files' tropes found in the other entries. It maintains a deadpan tone throughout and avoids the common AI pitfall of over-explaining the satire, instead allowing the grotesque visual of the human-filing cabinet to carry the joke.
